topic: Dementia diagnosis and treatment in memory services

audits.title: Clinical Audit of the Quality of Care Delivered by Community Mental Health Services for Older People to People Living With Dementia and Their Carers
audits.standard: NICE 2018 dementia guideline and TEWV 2019 person-centred dementia care pathway
audits.setting: Community Mental Health Services for Older People, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Consent recorded 80%; prognosis information 47%; dementia and driving 26%; accessible information leaflets 16%; carer's assessment offered 26%

audits.intervention: Action plans on areas needing improvement (not detailed)

cycle2.result: Consent recorded 65%; prognosis information 80%; dementia and driving 53%; accessible leaflets 50%; carer's assessment offered 18%

audits.other_findings: Consent recording and carer's assessments fell; COVID-19 lockdown thought to have limited leaflet sharing in the first cycle.
audits.citation: Ohioma K, Pearce S. Clinical Audit of the Quality of Care Delivered by Community Mental Health Services for Older People to People Living With Dementia and Their Carers. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S173-S174.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Dementia Diagnosis and Management – According to Disease Severity
audits.standard: NICE NG97 (1.5): consider memantine with acetylcholinesterase inhibitor in moderate to severe Alzheimer's dementia; Trust guidelines

cycle1.result: Severity documented in only 7% (all moderate), 93% generic diagnosis; 46/60 on medication, all on monotherapy; 46 completed the diagnostic pathway.

audits.other_findings: Mixed dementia 40%, Alzheimer's 39%, Lewy body 8% of diagnoses. Combination therapy not yet considered at diagnosis.
audits.citation: Fatunla S. Clinical Audit of Dementia Diagnosis and Management – According to Disease Severity. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S232-S232. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.568.

audits.title: Trustwide Clinical Audit of Dementia Diagnosis: How Are Diagnoses Made and What Treatments Are Offered?
audits.standard: NICE NG97 (2018) and TEWV Dementia Pathway: diagnostic work-up, subtype diagnosis, cholinesterase inhibitors/memantine and cognitive stimulation therapy
audits.setting: 15 memory services, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Dementia subtype given in 100%; medication offered when indicated in 96% (10 of 15 services 100%).

audits.other_findings: Only 2 services offered cognitive stimulation therapy to all suitable patients; 10 teams scored below 40%.
audits.citation: Sodiya O, Atewogboye O, Ataria R, Krishnan M, Raw R. Trustwide Clinical Audit of Dementia Diagnosis: How Are Diagnoses Made and What Treatments Are Offered?. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S218-S219. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10552.

audits.title: Drugs for dementia: the first year. An audit of prescribing practice.
audits.standard: Department of Health and Social Services (March 1998) prescribing guidelines for drugs for dementia

cycle1.result: Guidelines generally followed; 3 patients prescribed drugs outside the guidelines; most failures (10) were due to poor recording of data in the clinical record.

audits.intervention: Changes made to documentation of patient assessments; suggestions made to review CREST guidelines.
audits.other_findings: No agreed shared care protocols had been implemented despite DHSS recommendation, but this did not seem to affect access to the drugs.
audits.citation: McGirr G, Compton SA. Drugs for dementia: the first year. An audit of prescribing practice. Ulster Med J. 2000;69(2):123-127. PMID: 11196723.

audits.title: The London memory service audit and quality improvement programme.
audits.setting: Ten London memory services, case note review

cycle1.result: Variation in neuroimaging practice, neuropsychology referrals, diagnosis subtype, non-dementia diagnoses, waiting times and post-diagnostic support.

audits.intervention: Four service improvement projects initiated from audit findings.
audits.other_findings: Recommends streamlined pathways, pathways for patients without dementia and monitoring appropriateness of neuroimaging.
audits.citation: Cook LD, Nichol KE, Isaacs JD. The London memory service audit and quality improvement programme. BJPsych Bull. 2019;43(5):215-220. doi:10.1192/bjb.2019.18. PMID: 30898180.
